hero.subtitle: A fall at a Covina store, sidewalk, or apartment complex can leave you with medical bills and unanswered questions. We connect you at no cost with an independent attorney who handles premises liability cases across Covina and the surrounding San Gabriel Valley.

about.title: Covina Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Covina's mix of retail centers along Citrus Avenue, older apartment buildings near Badillo Street, and busy foot traffic around San Bernardino Road all create the kind of everyday hazards that lead to falls: wet floors left unmarked, cracked pavement never repaired, poor lighting in stairwells, or loose flooring in a store aisle. Under California law, a property owner or manager isn't automatically responsible just because someone fell on their property. The injured person generally has to show the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the dangerous condition and didn't fix it or warn people about it. That's why what happens right after a fall matters so much. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle your case directly; we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney in our network who can evaluate what happened, help gather evidence like surveillance footage before it's deleted, and advise you on next steps.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before It's Too Late

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. An attorney can help identify maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records that speak to that knowledge.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Covina stores and apartment complexes overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that video can be critical to supporting a claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you're found partly responsible for a fall, California's pure comparative fault rule means you may still recover a portion of damages. An attorney can help present the facts fairly instead of letting an insurer assign you most of the blame.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Covina?
items.answer: In general, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit for injuries against a private property owner. If the property is owned by a government entity, such as a city building or public sidewalk, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim, so it's worth getting guidance sooner rather than later.

items.question: I fell at a shopping center near Citrus Avenue — what should I do first?
items.answer: Try to document the exact spot where you fell, take photos of any spill, crack, or hazard, and ask if there's a manager on duty who can create an incident report. If there were witnesses, get their names, and consider asking the business to preserve any surveillance footage before it's routinely deleted.

items.question: Does it matter if I wasn't watching where I was walking?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California follows a pure comparative fault system, meaning you can still pursue compensation even if you were partly at fault, though your recovery may be reduced by your percentage of responsibility. An independent attorney can help evaluate the full picture rather than accepting an insurer's initial assessment of blame.
